architecture.text:
PART 1 — ARCHITECTURE SUMMARY (plain text, no markdown bold)

PRODUCT IDENTITY
- Headline/pitch: "Audit-Grade ESG Intelligence. In Days, Not Quarters." — an AI-powered platform unifying ESG, EHS, SDGs, CSR, and Sustainability into a single defensible Enterprise Impact Performance (EIP) score for board reporting, investor disclosure, and regulatory filings.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
- The page drives visitors toward two primary conversion actions: requesting a product demo ("Request Demo") and reading supporting methodology documentation ("Read the EIP Methodology"). Secondary objectives include establishing credibility with enterprise sustainability leaders and communicating breadth of framework coverage to qualify prospects.

INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
- 1. Hero/Above-the-fold: Headline, sub-pitch, key stats (22 agents, 5 domains, 16+ frameworks, 1 EIP score), and dual CTAs anchoring the value proposition.
- 2. Framework Coverage: Horizontal signal bar listing supported standards (GRI, CSRD, TCFD, SASB, ISO, CDP) with a "enter once, map everywhere" message, followed by placeholder partner logos.
- 3. Social Proof / Customer Evidence: One real testimonial (Victor Udo, Bucknell University) and two pending enterprise testimonial slots, plus a case study headline.
- 4. Platform Intelligence / Agent Catalog: Two-tier breakdown of 22 AI agents across 5 domain-specialist agents and 10+ cross-domain operational agents, including KPI alerts, materiality matrix, and EIP Score agent.
- 5. Practitioner Workflows, Sector Coverage, and Bottom CTA: Eight named practitioner tools, an agentic workflow diagram, four industry verticals with "Learn more" links, a repeat demo CTA block, and a security/compliance footer signal strip.

CONTENT INVENTORY
- Visible CTAs: "Request Demo", "Read the EIP Methodology", "Sign In", "Go to Home", "Mission Control →", "Learn more" (x4, one per sector vertical), "← Back"
- Visible forms or input affordances: No inline form fields are rendered in the captured body text; demo requests appear to route to a CTA button without an embedded form visible in the snapshot.
- Trust signals: One named testimonial with credentials (Victor Udo, FNSE, PhD, Former Director of Sustainability, Bucknell University); claimed outcome stat ("~30% carbon reduction, Top-25 Green University ranking"); platform stats (22 AI agents, 5 domains, 16+ frameworks); security badges (TLS 1.3, AES-256, GDPR-Ready, Audit Log, Multi-tenant Architecture, SSO Ready); cost/confidence claims ("Cut ESG reporting cost by 60%, Raise audit confidence by 100%"); SOC 2 Type II readiness in progress disclosure; five placeholder enterprise partner logo slots (unconfirmed); two pending enterprise testimonial slots.

TECH SIGNALS
- JS-rendered page (browserless capture method confirms client-side rendering dependency, likely React or a similar SPA framework).
- Language switcher present (EN/Español/Français), suggesting i18n middleware or a localization library.
- Multi-tenant architecture explicitly stated, implying cloud-hosted SaaS backend.
- TLS 1.3 in-transit and AES-256 at-rest encryption signals modern cloud infrastructure (likely AWS, GCP, or Azure).
- No explicit CDN, framework version, or build tool signals visible in the body text.
- "Built by VEU AI Studio" attribution suggests a boutique dev studio rather than a standard no-code platform.

ACCESSIBILITY SIGNALS
- Heading hierarchy has notable irregularities: the page jumps from h1 to h3 ("One Platform. Every Major Framework.") before using h2, which breaks sequential heading order and may confuse screen readers.
- Multiple h3 headings are used for agent names and feature names beneath h2 sections — structurally reasonable but dependent on correct DOM nesting not fully verifiable from the snippet.
- No alt-text evidence visible for partner/customer logos; placeholder logo text ("[ENTERPRISE PARTNER LOGO PENDING]") suggests images may lack meaningful alt attributes.
- No explicit ARIA landmark or skip-nav signals present in the captured text.
- Contrast indicators cannot be assessed from text capture alone.

QUALITY SCORE: 54/100
- The page communicates a sophisticated, well-structured product concept with clear agent taxonomy and framework coverage, but is significantly undermined by multiple placeholder trust signals (unconfirmed logos, pending testimonials), a broken heading hierarchy, no visible embedded form, unverified performance claims with only one real customer reference, and incomplete social proof that reduces credibility for an enterprise-targeting product.

---

improvement_plan.text:
PART 1 — IMPROVEMENT PLAN (plain text, no markdown bold)

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The single biggest opportunity is converting the two pending enterprise testimonial slots and five placeholder partner logos into real social proof, as enterprise buyers require peer-validated credibility before engaging sales — without this, the sophisticated agent taxonomy and EIP methodology claims feel unsubstantiated and will suppress demo request conversions. The single biggest risk is that the combination of visible placeholder text ("[ENTERPRISE PARTNER LOGO PENDING]", "[ENTERPRISE TESTIMONIAL PENDING — contact sales@saige.com to be featured]") rendered on a live production page actively signals to enterprise prospects that the product is pre-launch or unproven, creating the opposite of the audit-grade trust the headline promises and potentially disqualifying SAIGE before a single demo is booked.

PRIORITIZED IMPROVEMENTS (max 7)

[P0] [trust] Remove or gate all visible placeholder content — Replace "[ENTERPRISE PARTNER LOGO PENDING]" logo slots and "[ENTERPRISE TESTIMONIAL PENDING]" blocks with either real references or a single honest statement such as "Reference clients available under NDA — contact sales" to stop the page from broadcasting unfinished state to every enterprise visitor who lands on it.

[P0] [conversion] Embed a lightweight inline demo request form in the hero — The current "Request Demo" CTA routes away from the page with no visible form; adding a 3-field inline form (Name, Work Email, Company Size) directly beneath the hero subheading removes a full navigation step and captures intent at peak attention.

[P1] [trust] Secure and prominently display at least two named enterprise testimonials with verifiable titles, company names, and outcome metrics — The single Victor Udo reference is credible but is framed as "SAIGE-style methodology" rather than direct platform use, which a skeptical enterprise buyer will notice; two Fortune 500 or public-sector CSO quotes with specific quantified outcomes would dramatically shift conversion.

[P1] [technical] Fix the heading hierarchy from h1 → h3 → h2 — The page jumps directly from the h1 hero headline to an h3 ("One Platform. Every Major Framework.") before introducing h2 elements, breaking WCAG 1.3.1 and degrading screen reader navigation; change the framework coverage heading to h2 and audit all subsequent heading levels to enforce a strict sequential order.

[P1] [copy] Rewrite the cost and confidence claims with sourcing transparency — "Cut ESG reporting cost by 60%" and "Raise audit confidence by 100%" are high-impact claims currently footnoted only as "based on EIP methodology benchmarks"; replace the footnote with a linked methodology PDF excerpt or a named pilot customer outcome to give procurement and legal reviewers a reference they can validate.

[P2] [design] Add meaningful alt text and confirmed logos to all image slots — Placeholder logo images with no alt text fail WCAG 1.1.1 and signal incomplete build to assistive technology users; even temporarily replacing logo slots with a "Trusted by organizations in energy, higher education, and public sector" text strip is preferable to broken or empty image states.

[P2] [conversion] Add a persistent sticky navigation bar with a single high-contrast "Request Demo" CTA — The page is content-dense (22 agents, 8 practitioner tools, 4 sector verticals) and the primary CTA appears only at the hero and the bottom block; a sticky nav ensures the conversion action is always one click away regardless of scroll depth.

QUICK WINS (max 3)

Remove all five "[ENTERPRISE PARTNER LOGO PENDING]" placeholder strings and replace with a two-line text note ("Partner logos confirmed upon agreement — inquire at sales@saige.com") or simply hide the logo row until real assets are available — this takes under 15 minutes and immediately stops the page from advertising its own incompleteness.

Change the h3 "One Platform. Every Major Framework." heading tag to h2 in the HTML/JSX source — a one-line code edit that corrects the heading hierarchy violation, improves screen reader navigation, and removes a WCAG non-conformance without any visual design change.

Add a disclaimer anchor link to the "60% cost reduction" and "100% audit confidence" headline claims pointing to the existing EIP methodology page — a one-line copy and link addition that transforms unverified marketing assertions into substantiated references and reduces legal exposure.

STRUCTURAL CHANGES (max 3)

Redesign the social proof section as a living evidence hub: replace the static testimonial layout with a structured case study card format showing industry vertical, framework used, quantified outcome, and verifiable attribution — this requires design and copywriting effort but is the highest-leverage trust-building change available given the enterprise audience and the current proof vacuum.

Build and embed a native inline demo request form with progressive disclosure (step 1: email and company size; step 2: industry and framework interest; step 3: preferred date) replacing the current external CTA redirect — this requires frontend engineering but eliminates the drop-off point between intent and capture and enables immediate lead segmentation by sector and framework need.

Implement a semantic, accessible component architecture audit: restructure the heading hierarchy across the full page DOM, add ARIA landmark roles (main, navigation, region) to major page sections, ensure all decorative and informational images have appropriate alt attributes, and add a visible skip-to-content link — this requires a focused engineering sprint but establishes the accessibility baseline expected by government and public sector buyers who are explicitly listed as a target vertical.

QUALITY SCORE: 81/100
